- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing near-term price spikes.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 70+), model forecasts overshoot or fail to peak accurately, often peaking too early or too high.
- Model shows weak mean reversion — fails to anticipate sharp reversals or corrections after peaks.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the first 10 days, then become more aggressive — possibly due to misjudging volatility or momentum.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of late-period price increases (last 5–10 days), especially when true prices rise sharply.
- Forecasts often fail to capture the “tail” of the distribution — i.e., the final 5–10 days where true prices are highest.
- Model exhibits bias toward lower values, especially when historical mean is above 68 — suggesting a systematic underestimation of upward momentum.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to reflect volatility clustering or sudden jumps in price.
- Model tends to overcorrect after minor dips, leading to overshoots in subsequent days.
